opportunity: Datatype::type_order ranks SUB_UINT_PLAIN (16) ahead of SUB_INT_PLAIN (17), so in get_local_type's most-specific fold one uint vote outranks every int vote on a Varnode and nothing downstream re-decides. On -O2 x86-64 those uint votes are structural (INT_ZEXT from a 32-bit instruction widening into its 64-bit register; INT_AND/INT_RIGHT/INT_XOR from a strength-reduced loop), so a counter compiled from `int` is declared `unsigned int` and cast back to `int` at every comparison.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-signedness.xml (two functions, 6 assertions: the masked loop bound two-pass, and the sub-int width guard reduced from findutils find -O2 sub_bac0) + tests/stages/kuna-signedness-int16.xml (two functions, 4 assertions: the same width guard on x86:LE:16:Protected Mode, whose own cspec integer_size is 2, with a 4-byte control that does flip) + 10 unit tests in p9_emit/kuna_typeround/tests.rs
inspiration: TRex (Bosamiya, Woo, Parno; USENIX Security 2025) sections 3.3.5 and 5.1 -- type rounding decides signedness after propagation from the accumulated size-tagged operation set, with a flag preferring signed for the ambiguous case
trex_note: Re-derived from the paper and from reading https://github.com/secure-foundations/trex (BSD-3). No TRex code is copied, so no NOTICE entry or per-file attribution header is added. Two classification points were taken from reading trex/src/structural.rs: `ZeroExtendTgt => None` (a zero-extension describes the source operand's type, not the widened value's) and the signed/unsigned collapse preference used by `collapse_union_of_signed_and_unsigned_ints`.

syntax_pair.why: the round-2 run was `gcc -fsyntax-only -w` filtered to `error:` lines. `-w` disables every warning, so it could not observe -Wsign-compare or -Wsign-conversion -- the only diagnostics this feature can move. It proved `no new compile ERROR`, which was never in dispute.

executable_round_trip.harness: .scratch/roundtrip4.py -- both texts in one program (renamed apart), deterministic stubs for every undefined callee, a shared 4 MiB arena behind every synthesized global, 2000 pseudo-random input vectors per function, comparing the return value and a hash of the arena plus the stub trace

prefer_signed.apparent_differ_note: ls sub_1b525 reports DIFFER on the RETURN VALUE only and reports the same DIFFER when the upstream text is compared against itself (round-2 control): the function returns a real malloc() pointer, so two successive calls cannot return the same address. The arena hash is 50e4f77d30cef1d9 in both arms.
prefer_signed.note: the run was stopped after 112 of 270 functions; the warning oracle above covers all 270

prefer_unsigned.note: the run was stopped after 221 of 737 functions; the warning oracle above covers all 737

executable_round_trip.coverage_note: this is the narrowest of the three correctness instruments and its coverage is stated with every number: most changed functions do not compile out of context at all (a Ghidra idiom like `v41._0_1_`, a dat_ global used as both scalar and pointer, a goto into another scope), identically in both arms.

correctness_evidence.declaration_vs_cast_contradiction: none by construction: a cast is dropped only when the emitter actually wrote the rounded type as that high's declaration and the cast target is that exact type, so the surviving expression has the same C type it had.
correctness_evidence.ubsan: gcc -O2 -fsanitize=undefined on an early draft's zlib sub_ce20 text reported `left shift of negative value` where a left-shifted `unsigned int` had been re-declared `int`. INT_LEFT operand 0 is an unsigned demand for that reason among others (see int_left_rule), and zlib's bit accumulators no longer move.

differential_warning_oracle.method: every function whose emitted C changed is compiled before and after with the SAME synthesized extern declarations and `gcc -fsyntax-only -std=gnu89 -Wsign-compare -Wsign-conversion`, and the WARNING sets are diffed. gcc's column is used to read the operator the warning points at, so an ordered comparison is distinguished from an equality even on a line containing both. Harness: .scratch/signwarn.py
differential_warning_oracle.the_deltas: all 24 are on `==`/`!=` -- `if (v3 == strlen(v1))`, `if (v1 != -1)`, `while (v2 != v5)`, `return a0[4] == v3;` -- which is benign at a fixed width: both operands convert to the same width and the bit patterns compared are identical. 0 are on `< <= > >=`, which is the number that would say a comparison changed meaning.
differential_warning_oracle.sign_conversion_deltas: expected by construction and reported separately: re-declaring a local changes the conversion at its assignments, call arguments and returns, all same-width and therefore bit-identical. auto 58/+ 39/-, prefer-signed 295/+ 104/-, prefer-unsigned 519/+ 168/-.
differential_warning_oracle.left_shift_check: no variable any value declares signed is ever the left operand of `<<` in the emitted text: 29 newly-signed declarations under auto, 332 under prefer-signed, 10 in zlib libz -O2, 0 shiftees (.scratch/shiftcheck.py)

speed_note: the default flip re-measured on the shipped build: interleaved min-of-15 whole-binary `decompile-all` on coreutils fmt, ls and sort at -O2, each iteration running `--option signedness upstream` and then the default (auto) back to back (.scratch/speed-r6.sh, .scratch/speed-r6.log). Per-binary minima: fmt 4.1255s -> 4.1235s (-0.05%), ls 13.7452s -> 13.4545s (-2.11%), sort 15.0587s -> 14.3831s (-4.49%); summed, 32.929s -> 31.961s, -2.94%. Two of the three deltas are NEGATIVE, which a pass that only adds work cannot be: the effect is below this box's noise floor under the other agents' load, not a speedup. The medians say the same thing from the other side (fmt +5.10%, ls -0.22%, sort -1.52%) and are not usable here. The tightest measurement taken on this feature -- min-of-21 on fmt alone, at a quieter moment -- was +0.17%, which is the number to believe for the cost; either way it is inside the +5% budget. The pass is one walk over each declared integer high's readers per function, plus a HashMap lookup per cast, and `option signedness upstream` short-circuits all of it on the first `is_active` test.

dwarf_accuracy.method: 238 unstripped DWARF twins (the compiled/ binaries beside the stripped images decbench scores) across coreutils, grep, gzip, diffutils, bzip2, findutils and tar at -O0 and -O2. Whole-image decompile-all once per value; every plain-integer local declaration whose name DWARF also knows INSIDE THE SAME FUNCTION, at the same width, is compared against the DWARF base type's encoding. Signedness is binary, so a declaration that differs between two values is right in exactly one of them.
dwarf_accuracy.harness: .scratch/acc/dwarfsign.py (pyelftools DIE walk, follows typedef/const/volatile and DW_AT_abstract_origin) + .scratch/acc/accuracy_r5.py
dwarf_accuracy.caveat: Only names DWARF knows in the same function are compared. kuna also names some register locals after the parameter of the function they feed, where the ground truth can be genuinely ambiguous (ls/du save_abbr's `abbr_size` is extend_abbrs's size_t parameter, while the value's own source identity in save_abbr is the SIGNED idx_t zone_size that C converts at the call). Those are excluded rather than scored either way.
dwarf_accuracy.coverage_caveat: the oracle can only score a declaration kuna names the way DWARF does in the same function, which is overwhelmingly a stack local: 5,308 of the 6,259 comparable rows are -O0 and 951 are -O2, while the defect this option exists for is an -O2 register local. auto moves 4 of them (1 at -O0, 3 at -O2) out of 575 flips image-wide -- 0.7% coverage -- so auto's fidelity is UNMEASURED and its +0.1pp is noise at that count. prefer-signed moves 386 (134 + 252) and is the only value with a real measurement. Not a DWARF type-lock artifact: on fmt -O2 auto flips 4 of 132 plain-integer declarations unstripped and 4 of 223 stripped.

control_all_signed.what: declare EVERY eligible plain-integer local signed, no operation walk at all -- same candidate set, same width guard, same declaration-ownership guard, evidence deleted. NOT a shipped value: built from the same source through the measurement-only escape hatch KUNA_MEAS_ALLSIGNED, which exists in .scratch/measbin/kuna and in no committed file (that binary is byte-identical to the shipped one with the variable unset, verified on 32 whole-image dumps).
control_all_signed.why: prefer-signed is auto plus one line ('declare an unobserved value signed'), so the reviewer's question is whether the walk in front of that line does anything a one-line tie-break would not.
control_all_signed.answer: it does. The control scores 92.8% overall and 59.2% at -O2 -- BELOW leaving the declarations alone (71.9%) -- against prefer-signed's 98.4% / 94.8%. Of its 790 DWARF-judged flips 376 are right and 414 wrong; 379 of the wrong ones are size_t locals declared int, against prefer-signed's 12. The unsigned demands the walk collects (an unsigned compare, >>, / %, ZEXT) are what holds size_t unsigned, and they are the whole difference between 98.4% and 92.8%.

declaration_ownership_guard.what: SignPlan::retain_sole_named -- the plan is filtered to highs whose rendered name is unique on the printer's candidate list, before any declaration collapse runs.
declaration_ownership_guard.why: the composite-Symbol retain, collapse_symbol_decls, DeclDedup and the local_name_aliases group suppression each fold several highs onto ONE declaration line, and each pairs candidates by NAME. A rounded type reaching those decisions could move a collapse key (splitting a declaration that used to collapse) or re-sign the single line a non-flipped sibling's uses read through. record_applied already refused the CAST drop in those cases; the declaration line was not guarded.
declaration_ownership_guard.cost_sweep_fmt_ls_sort_du_O0_O2: 0 bytes -- all 32 whole-binary dumps byte-identical to the pre-guard build under every value

group_piece_alias (the case it exists fo: cp overwrite_ok @0x67a0 v1 and make_dir_parents_private @0x4b10 v2
cases.group_piece_alias_shape: a VariableGroup whose byte pieces all render ONE name and read through ONE declaration line (`v1._0_1_ = x->copy_as_regular, v1._1_1_ = ...`); flipping the line they alias through has no evidence behind it.
cases.conservative_decline: shuf sparse_swap @0x6e6f v1 -- two highs both named v1 on the candidate list survive every collapse and the printer's uniqueness pass renames one to v1_1, so this flip would have been safe. 1 spurious decline per 238 binaries is the price of a filter readable off the candidate list alone.

promotion_width_guard.rule: a declaration narrower than max(4, TypeFactory::get_size_of_int()) is never re-signed
promotion_width_guard.why_not_the_target: the promotion runs in the compiler that READS the emitted C, where int is 4 bytes. The target cspec's <data_organization><integer_size> is 2 on avr8egcc, avr8gcc, TI_MSP430, TI_MSP430X, CR16, PIC24 and x86-16, so a target-derived guard re-signed a 2-byte local there and brought the findutils find -O2 sub_bac0 defect back.
promotion_width_guard.proof: tests/stages/kuna-signedness-int16.xml scores 2/4 with the target-derived guard (`int2 v1;` becomes `uint2 v1;` under prefer-unsigned while `if (v1 != -1)` stays) and 4/4 with max(4, ...). Measured by building both, not argued.
promotion_width_guard.corpus_caveat: the 238-binary DWARF corpus is entirely 4-byte-int targets, so its `0 sub-int flips` cannot distinguish the two guards; the stage test is what distinguishes them.

int_left_rule.status: a stated PREFERENCE, not a soundness requirement: `a << k` shifts the same bits either way and INT_LEFT takes the default getInputCast arm (care_uint_int = false). The earlier `negative << k is UB` justification is withdrawn -- signed overflow of `+ - *` is UB on the same footing and those are neutral.
kept_because: a value the body ORs and shifts left is a bit buffer, which C source spells unsigned (zlib deflate sub_ce20/sub_d3c0)
a signed `<<` is the one otherwise-neutral operator -fsanitize=undefined reports

int_left_rule.review_claim_refuted: the round-2 review attributed auto's six `int -> unsigned int` flips to this rule. They do not come from it: with the rule removed all six remain. int_left_rule.also_carries: the walk continues through it, so `(v << 3) >> 2` is decided by the `>>`

care_uint_int_claim.corrected: the demand set is a strict SUPERSET of the ops whose get_input_cast passes care_uint_int = true. The four ordered comparisons, / %, >> and the two extensions pass true; INT_SCARRY/INT_SBORROW/INT_CARRY, a same-width CPUI_CAST and INT_LEFT all fall through to the dispatch's DEFAULT arm, which passes false (decompiler/crates/kuna-decomp/src/p9_emit/coreaction_casts.rs, get_input_cast).
care_uint_int_claim.why_it_is_still_sound: demanding on the carry intrinsics and on a same-width cast is an over-constraint, not a gap -- a carry intrinsic spells its own signedness in its name and a cast token establishes the type it prints -- so it can only ever DECLINE a flip that upstream's own flag would have allowed. Soundness rests on the NEUTRAL list being signedness-independent at a fixed width; care_uint_int corroborates where upstream draws the same line but does not prove it.
